To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) voltage/frequency scaling of CPUs and communication links can be done in a coordinated fashion to maximize energy savings, (ii) the proposed algorithm is very effective in reducing energy consumption of sparse matrix computations, and (iii) the energy savings are consistent with different network sizes and voltage/frequency levels.

the proposed integrated CPU/link voltage scaling algorithm brings up to 17% energy saving compared to the pure CPU voltage scaling algorithm, and up to 13% energy saving compared with the pure network link voltage scaling algorithm, while keeping the execution time the same.

we have proposed and evaluated a new algorithm that scales CPU and communication link voltages simultaneously and our experimental results with tree-based sparse matrix applications show that the proposed approach can save up to 17% energy compared to the pure communication link voltage/frequency scaling.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the problem of reducing the power consumption of parallel applications.
the problem of reducing power consumption in parallel sparse matrix computations.
the energy efficiency of high-performance parallel computing systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
our integrated voltage scaling approach brings 20% energy savings on average over the pure CPU voltage scaling and 30% over the pure link voltage scaling.
the proposed approach can be used as a powerful tool to achieve energy savings in a mesh network with a very small overhead.
the proposed integrated approach is very effective and brings 13%-17% energy savings on top of pure voltage scaling approaches.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
our approach can be used as a complementary technique to the existent CPU and communication link voltage scaling techniques.
we propose and evaluate a novel integrated voltage scaling approach that scales CPU and network simultaneously.

our integrated voltage/frequency scaling approach for CPUs and links in a parallel computing platform is a simple and effective solution that is able to reduce the energy consumption of the system by 13%-17% without impacting the application execution times.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the integrated link/CPU voltage/frequency scaling is an effective way to reduce energy consumption of parallel applications.
the proposed approach is very effective and can be applied on different parallel applications to reduce energy consumption of parallel platforms.
the proposed integrated CPU/communication link voltage scaling approach can be used to effectively reduce energy consumption of parallel applications.
